beginner.headline: Don Toliver Moves Two London Shows to Later Dates
beginner.brief: US rapper Don Toliver has moved two London shows to later dates. An unknown substance, or type of material, was released into the crowd at his Manchester concert. The people at the concert had to leave on Sunday. The equipment is still in Manchester and cannot reach London in time for this week's shows. The Wembley show will now be on 14 December. The O2 show will now be on 15 December. Police said 12,000 people had to leave the arena, a large building for events. One person went to hospital. Police said 89 people had signs of illness after the concert. Fans at the Manchester show will get all their ticket money back.

intermediate.headline: Don Toliver postpones London shows after Manchester evacuation
intermediate.brief: US rapper Don Toliver has postponed two London shows after an unknown substance was released at his Manchester concert on Sunday. Live Nation said his stage equipment remained in Manchester and could not be moved in time for the London shows. The Wembley Arena performance has been rescheduled for 14 December, while The O2 show will take place on 15 December. Police said 12,000 people were evacuated, meaning they were moved out of the arena for safety. According to police, one person was taken to hospital and 89 people showed symptoms believed to be linked to exposure. Some fans reported problems with their eyes and breathing, according to the ambulance service. Police are testing items from the venue to identify the substance, and no arrests have been made. Some fans complained about security and a lack of searches as people entered the Manchester concert. The reported security system used technology to detect banned items without requiring people to empty their pockets. A statement said everyone with a ticket for the Manchester show would receive a full refund automatically. Toliver said he wanted to make sure everyone was safe and that the next show went ahead properly.

advanced.headline: Don Toliver delays London shows after Manchester arena evacuation
advanced.brief: Don Toliver postponed two London performances after his Manchester concert was evacuated on Sunday following the release of an unidentified substance into the audience. Live Nation attributed the London disruption to a logistical constraint: the stage and production equipment remained in Manchester and could not be moved in time for Monday's O2 performance or Tuesday's Wembley Arena show. Wembley Arena's replacement date is 14 December, while The O2 performance has been moved to 15 December. Police said 89 people displayed symptoms believed to be linked to contact with the substance, and one person was taken to hospital. Greater Manchester Police declared a major incident and said 12,000 people were evacuated from the arena. A further 88 people underwent dry decontamination, a procedure for removing contamination without water, and were subsequently accommodated at the Etihad Stadium while the incident was managed, police said. Fans described distressing scenes, while police initially suspected that the substance was tear gas. Police were continuing to test items at the arena to identify the substance, and no arrests had been made. Investigators were seeking to establish the substance's nature, its origin and any associated risk, according to Assistant Chief Constable Tom Harding. The question of whether any criminality had occurred was also under investigation. Some fans questioned security arrangements, complaining about a lack of searches as people entered the Manchester concert.
